text: Git/GitHub/CI-CD Lesson 19 had a workflow run tests automatically on every commit. The same pattern applies to infrastructure: run terraform plan automatically on every pull request.
The plan output — the actual computed diff — sits right there in the PR for review, not buried on someone's laptop where nobody else can see it before merge.
Merging to main should trigger apply, but not without a person saying so. GitHub's environment setting requires a reviewer's approval before that job proceeds.
Both workflows need Azure credentials. A service principal's client ID, secret, tenant ID, and subscription ID live as CI secrets, injected at run time, never committed to code.
Plan on every PR, a human gate before apply, credentials as secrets. Chapter 4 is done — next up, Chapter 5: this course's capstone.
